explain.say: Mars's rocks contain plenty of iron. Long ago, when Mars had water, the iron reacted with water and oxygen to make iron oxide, the same reddish stuff as the rust on an old bike.

faq.a: Its surface is covered in dust rich in iron oxide, a kind of rust. Iron oxide reflects red and orange light, so the planet looks red.
asks: Why is Mars called the red planet?

faq.a: In a way, yes. The red colour comes from iron oxides that formed when iron in Martian rocks reacted with water and oxygen, much as rust forms on iron here. Under the dusty top layer, many Martian rocks are dark grey.
asks: What is Mars's dust made of?

faq.q: How big are dust storms on Mars?
faq.a: Most are local, but every few years dust storms can wrap the whole planet for weeks. A global storm in 2018 blocked so much sunlight that the solar-powered Opportunity rover shut down for good.
asks: Can dust storms cover all of Mars?

faq.q: What colour is the sky on Mars?
faq.a: By day, fine dust makes the Martian sky a hazy butterscotch or pinkish colour. At sunset it turns bluish around the Sun, the opposite of Earth.

faq.q: Why was Mars named after a god of war?
faq.a: Its blood-red colour reminded ancient peoples of war and fire. The Romans named it after Mars, their god of war, and its two moons, Phobos and Deimos, mean fear and dread.

facts: Mars's red colour comes from iron oxides in its surface dust.
A planet-wide dust storm in 2018 ended NASA's Opportunity rover mission.
Mars has two small moons, Phobos and Deimos.
